This is a league based game.

For this first league, two drones race on an open track, without collisions. Fly through the gates, in order, in the right direction.

 The Goal

Pilot a racing drone through the gates of light of an indoor arena. Finish 3 laps before your opponents.

 Rules

The arena is a box: x from 0 to 12000 (east), y from 0 to 12000 (north), z from 0 (the floor) to 5000 (the ceiling). Walls and ceiling bounce you back, without damage.

Gates are rings of radius 800, each with a centre and a direction n. To clear your next gate, fly through its ring in the direction of n, with your whole drone inside the ring: your centre must pass less than 600 from the gate centre. Touching the ring, flying outside it or backwards does nothing. Gate 0 is the start and finish line, and a lap ends at gate 0.

Start: the drones sit on the floor near gate 0, 450 apart, all at the same distance from gate 1 and facing it. Gate 1 is always less than 4000 away horizontally from gate 0.

Your drone is a sphere of radius 200 with a radio: each turn you set THROTTLE (0 to 100), YAW, PITCH and ROLL (-100 to 100). The motors push along the drone's up axis. Gravity pulls it down. The drone keeps its speed from turn to turn. To fly forward, tilt the drone and add throttle.

The radio

The sticks follow the usual Mode 2 radio layout, which is fixed: the left stick is THROTTLE (up and down) and YAW (left and right), the right stick is PITCH (up and down) and ROLL (left and right).


What each stick does, in ANGLE mode.

  • ANGLE mode (the default, self-levelling): PITCH and ROLL set how far the drone leans (up to 60°, positive pitch leans forward, positive roll leans right) and YAW turns it (up to 30° per turn, positive turns right). The drone turns towards that attitude at up to 30° per turn. Centred sticks bring the drone back level.
  • ACRO mode (the racing mode): the sticks set rotation speeds around the drone's own axes, up to 60° per turn each. PITCH turns the nose down (positive) or up around the drone's right axis, ROLL rolls it right (positive) or left around its forward axis, and YAW spins it right (positive) or left around its up axis. Centred sticks keep the current attitude: nothing levels the drone for you. There is no tilt limit, so you can lean past 60° for more forward push (losing height), or flip. It is harder, but faster once you master it.

You choose the flight mode, ANGLE (the default) or ACRO, by writing it at the start of your first output. It stays for the whole race.

Tip: start with ANGLE. It keeps the drone stable and is the easiest way to get round the track. ACRO can be faster, since it leans further and turns quicker, but it is much harder to master: come back to it once your bot races well.

Camera: output CAM angle to tilt your FPV camera up from the drone's nose, from 0 to 60 degrees (default 30). It only changes what the viewer shows, not the race. Like on a real racing drone: to fly fast, the drone leans far forward, so a camera pointing straight along the nose ends up looking at the floor. Tilting it up keeps the track ahead on screen when your bot flies fast and leans hard.

Battery: it loses 1 per turn. Clearing a gate recharges it to 100. At 0, the motors stop.

Floor: you can land and take off again. A drone that touches the floor faster than 150 downwards, or with its motors stopped, is destroyed.

Other drones: drones fly through each other.

Slipstream: flying close behind another drone lowers your drag (see Expert rules).

Victory Conditions

Finish 3 laps first. The race ends as soon as one drone finishes (drones finishing on the same turn tie), when every drone is destroyed, or after 600 turns. The other drones are ranked by gates cleared, then by distance to the centre of their next gate (taken when they were destroyed).
Invalid output or running out of time.

 What is in store for me in the higher leagues?

  • Wood 1: up to 4 drones per race, and drones bounce off each other.
  • Bronze: hard impacts CRASH both drones (motors off for a few turns), a BOOST, smaller gates, and tracks with ladders and hairpins.
  • Silver: power cells beside the track: CHARGE (an extra boost), SHIELD (no crashes) and GHOST (fly through drones), the last two kept until you USE them.
  • Gold: hold up to 2 boosts.
  • Legend: hold up to 3 boosts.

 Game Input

Initialization input
Line 1: playerCount myId laps gateCount
Next gateCount lines: x y z nx ny nz radius: centre (integers), direction and radius of gate 0, 1, ...
Next line: cellCount (always 0 in this league)
Next cellCount lines: x y z type (CHARGE, SHIELD or GHOST)
Input for one game turn
Next playerCount lines, one per drone in id order:
x y z vx vy vz: position and speed
fx fy fz ux uy uz: the drone's forward and up unit vectors
nextGate lap boosts boostTimer battery cutout state shield ghost item
(boostTimer: turns until the next boost comes back; cutout: turns left in a CRASH; state: 0 destroyed, 1 flying, 2 finished; shield, ghost: turns left; item: 0 none, 1 SHIELD, 2 GHOST)
boosts, boostTimer, cutout, shield and item are always 0 in this league.
ghost is always 0 in this league.
Next cellCount lines: respawnTimer (0 when the cell is there)
Output for one game turn
One line: THROTTLE YAW PITCH ROLL (integers; values out of range are clamped), optionally followed by CAM angle (FPV camera tilt in the viewer, 0 to 60), in any order, and a message. The first output may start with the flight mode: ANGLE (the default) or ACRO. Later outputs may repeat it, but the mode does not change.
Example: ANGLE 80 0 40 -10
Constraints
playerCount = 2
4 ≤ gateCount ≤ 6
Time: 28000 / playerCount ms in total for the whole race. Spend it as you like.

 Expert Rules

Right = f × u. Each turn, for every flying drone, in this order:

  1. Re-orthonormalise f then u (Gram-Schmidt).
  2. Motors stopped (empty battery): no rotation and no thrust. Otherwise:
  3. ANGLE rotation: heading = the direction of f seen from above (of u if f is vertical), turned right by YAW·30°/100. Target: start level, facing the heading; pitch the nose down by PITCH·60°/100; then tilt u towards the right by ROLL·60°/100 (forward unchanged). Rotate towards the target the shortest way, at most 30°; within 30°, take the target exactly.
  4. ACRO rotation: one rotation by the vector 60° × (−PITCH·right + ROLL·forward − YAW·up) / 100.
  5. v += u·50·THROTTLE/100 − (0, 0, 20).
  6. Move by v in a straight line. Collisions with walls, floor and other drones are handled in time order. Two drones collide only while they get closer; the impact speed is their relative speed along the line between their centres; they bounce elastically (equal masses). A destroyed drone stops. Gates are checked along the path.
  7. Slipstream: you are in the slipstream of another flying drone moving at 100 or more if you are at most 1500 behind it along its speed and within 300 of that line. Drag is then 0.9725, otherwise 0.97. v ×= drag.
  8. Round position and speed to 0.01, f and u to 0.000001 (half up).
  9. Battery: 100 if a gate was cleared this turn, otherwise −1.

The values you read are the exact game state. The referee's source code is public.

The arena is a box: x from 0 to 12000 (east), y from 0 to 12000 (north), z from 0 (the floor) to 5000 (the ceiling). Walls and ceiling bounce you back, without damage.

Gates are rings of radius 800, each with a centre and a direction n. To clear your next gate, fly through its ring in the direction of n, with your whole drone inside the ring: your centre must pass less than 600 from the gate centre. Touching the ring, flying outside it or backwards does nothing. Gate 0 is the start and finish line, and a lap ends at gate 0.

Start: the drones sit on the floor near gate 0, 450 apart, all at the same distance from gate 1 and facing it. Gate 1 is always less than 4000 away horizontally from gate 0.

The radio

The sticks follow the usual Mode 2 radio layout, which is fixed: the left stick is THROTTLE (up and down) and YAW (left and right), the right stick is PITCH (up and down) and ROLL (left and right).


What each stick does, in ANGLE mode.

  • ANGLE mode (the default, self-levelling): PITCH and ROLL set how far the drone leans (up to 60°, positive pitch leans forward, positive roll leans right) and YAW turns it (up to 30° per turn, positive turns right). The drone turns towards that attitude at up to 30° per turn. Centred sticks bring the drone back level.
  • ACRO mode (the racing mode): the sticks set rotation speeds around the drone's own axes, up to 60° per turn each. PITCH turns the nose down (positive) or up around the drone's right axis, ROLL rolls it right (positive) or left around its forward axis, and YAW spins it right (positive) or left around its up axis. Centred sticks keep the current attitude: nothing levels the drone for you. There is no tilt limit, so you can lean past 60° for more forward push (losing height), or flip. It is harder, but faster once you master it.

You choose the flight mode, ANGLE (the default) or ACRO, by writing it at the start of your first output. It stays for the whole race.

Like on a real racing drone: to fly fast, the drone leans far forward, so a camera pointing straight along the nose ends up looking at the floor. Tilting it up keeps the track ahead on screen when your bot flies fast and leans hard.

Floor: you can land and take off again. A drone that touches the floor faster than 150 downwards, or with its motors stopped, is destroyed.

Collisions: drones bounce off each other. At the start, every drone is a ghost for 30 turns: it flies through the other drones.

Slipstream: flying close behind another drone lowers your drag (see Expert rules).

Summary of new rules

You now hold up to 3 boosts.

 The Goal

Pilot a racing drone through the gates of light of an indoor arena. Finish 3 laps before your opponents.

 Rules

The arena is a box: x from 0 to 12000 (east), y from 0 to 12000 (north), z from 0 (the floor) to 5000 (the ceiling). Walls and ceiling bounce you back, without damage.

Gates are rings of radius 500, each with a centre and a direction n. To clear your next gate, fly through its ring in the direction of n, with your whole drone inside the ring: your centre must pass less than 300 from the gate centre. Touching the ring, flying outside it or backwards does nothing. Gate 0 is the start and finish line, and a lap ends at gate 0.

Start: the drones sit on the floor near gate 0, 450 apart, all at the same distance from gate 1 and facing it. Gate 1 is always less than 4000 away horizontally from gate 0.

Tracks can contain a ladder (two rings stacked on top of each other, flown in opposite directions) or a hairpin (two rings side by side, flown in opposite directions).

Your drone is a sphere of radius 200 with a radio: each turn you set THROTTLE (0 to 100), YAW, PITCH and ROLL (-100 to 100). The motors push along the drone's up axis. Gravity pulls it down. The drone keeps its speed from turn to turn. To fly forward, tilt the drone and add throttle.

The radio

The sticks follow the usual Mode 2 radio layout, which is fixed: the left stick is THROTTLE (up and down) and YAW (left and right), the right stick is PITCH (up and down) and ROLL (left and right).


What each stick does, in ANGLE mode.

  • ANGLE mode (the default, self-levelling): PITCH and ROLL set how far the drone leans (up to 60°, positive pitch leans forward, positive roll leans right) and YAW turns it (up to 30° per turn, positive turns right). The drone turns towards that attitude at up to 30° per turn. Centred sticks bring the drone back level.
  • ACRO mode (the racing mode): the sticks set rotation speeds around the drone's own axes, up to 60° per turn each. PITCH turns the nose down (positive) or up around the drone's right axis, ROLL rolls it right (positive) or left around its forward axis, and YAW spins it right (positive) or left around its up axis. Centred sticks keep the current attitude: nothing levels the drone for you. There is no tilt limit, so you can lean past 60° for more forward push (losing height), or flip. It is harder, but faster once you master it.

You choose the flight mode, ANGLE (the default) or ACRO, by writing it at the start of your first output. It stays for the whole race.

Camera: output CAM angle to tilt your FPV camera up from the drone's nose, from 0 to 60 degrees (default 30). It only changes what the viewer shows, not the race. Like on a real racing drone: to fly fast, the drone leans far forward, so a camera pointing straight along the nose ends up looking at the floor. Tilting it up keeps the track ahead on screen when your bot flies fast and leans hard.

Finish 3 laps first. The race ends as soon as one drone finishes (drones finishing on the same turn tie), when every drone is destroyed, or after 600 turns. The other drones are ranked by gates cleared, then by distance to the centre of their next gate (taken when they were destroyed).
